items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: Oh, yeah, I worked with Jelly. About, well, I went out two years with him. That's how I worked. See, Jelly, he would, in the wintertime, he'd take a band out.

ctx.x: Somebody once told me you worked with the Jelly Roll on the road.

Oh, yeah, I worked with Jelly. About, well, I went out two years with him. That's how I worked. See, Jelly, he would, in the wintertime, he'd take a band out. He'd go all over. Well, summer, he'd keep band together, but he wouldn't do much playing in the summer. But, I went out two years with him like that, the same way I did with Walter Barnes. He'd go out for the winter all down Florida and everywhere. But, when he'd come back, he had a big grocery in Chicago. Barnes, huh?
Barnes, Walter Barnes? Yeah, Walter Barnes.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Well, I didn't work with him but one year.

ctx.x: And when you worked with Jelly Roll, would you work all year round?

Well, I didn't work with him but one year. Jelly got down sick or something, and the next year, I don't know, even Bain had this winter part, you know. And Swayze, he taken sick and died. And that was one of Jelly boozing him in, you know. And the other deal was blown in Chicago, playing different spots all around like that. So that's how I let this happen. Jelly just passed out like that, and he died pretty soon. I believe he died in New York though. Didn't die in Chicago, died in New York. But now to tell the…
But when you worked with Jelly, was that after you went with Tiny Palm or before?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: He'd come on back to Chicago and he wouldn't take us out, you know. He didn't want no drinking.

ctx.x: Yeah, head, humble, dream, all them kind of things. And I played with a, Jerry Roe Morton, but let me tell you the funny, now you're all going to laugh about this. Jerry didn't want no drinking. I went to Jerry, man, tall boy, tall boy, I call him King Porter, trumpet player, meaning I was playing first and I was playing second. So Porter hit me and said, look at you, I said, man, we can drink. I said, how are we going to drink, man? He said, I'll show you. Came into the saloon, man, we got a flash, each one's…
But he didn't fight, didn't he? He'd come on back to Chicago and he wouldn't take us out, you know. He didn't want no drinking. Strictly didn't want no drinking.
Mr. Porter, did he write King Porter Stone?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: But John Jelly Roll after Cliff. Cliff wasn't there when I joined him.

ctx.x: But John Jelly Roll after Cliff. Cliff wasn't there when I joined him. But yeah, I saw him playing with Jelly Roll.

Did you know Hilaire Andrew? Sure, I knew Hilaire. He was a nice drummer. Where was he from? Here. And who did he play with in Lionhead? Did you know him back then? Well, Hilaire, I believe he played some too with this Jelly Roll.
